documents.title: Work Note
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - HR at work wants a note from my regular doctor saying I'm cleared for full duty now. The surgery office note only said light duty through Jan 3. Can you send one? Sorry for the short notice.

documents.title: Work Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done - letter attached to this message clearing you for full duty as of today. Your surgery clinic visit is Monday; they may give you their own note too. Glad you're feeling better.

documents.title: General Surgery - Post-op Visit
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward   Seen 1/7/2019

Two and a half weeks after laparoscopic appendectomy for acute appendicitis. She is back at work and feels well. No fever, eating normally. Port sites healed. Abdomen soft and nontender. Pathology reviewed with her - acute appendicitis without malignancy.

No restrictions. Discharged from surgical follow-up.

General Surgery

documents.title: Positive Pregnancy Test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two positive home tests this weekend!! Last period started Feb 9. What do I do next? Still on my prenatal and methadone like we talked about.

documents.title: Positive Pregnancy Test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Front desk will call to get you in this week. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin and keep your program dosing as is. Acetaminophen rather than sumatriptan for headaches if you can.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - New Pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: +HPT x2. LMP 2/9/19, regular cycles -> ~5w5d, EDD 11/16/19. No bleeding or pain. Taking prenatal vitamin daily. Methadone 60 mg via OTP - she let her counselor know yesterday. One migraine since LMP, used acetaminophen and it was enough.

O: Vitals ok. Urine hCG positive in office. Abdomen soft, NT.

A/P: Intrauterine pregnancy presumed, early. G1.
- Referred to OB; they see patients on methadone routinely and coordinate with the OTP.
- Continue methadone; do not taper. Continue prenatal vitamin.
- Headache: acetaminophen first; sumatriptan only if acetaminophen fails, occasional use.
- Call for bleeding or one-sided pain - first pregnancy, no prior ultrasound yet.
- Mood: reviewed her mom's postpartum depression; we'll keep an eye on it.

documents.title: Obstetrics - New Pregnancy Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward, DOB 10/16/1986

Seen 4/16/2019 for her initial prenatal visit at 9 weeks 3 days by LMP, consistent with exam. G1P0.

Medical history: migraine without aura; opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg daily via her treatment program; appendectomy 12/2018.
Medications: methadone 60 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, acetaminophen as needed; sumatriptan rarely.
Allergies: NKDA.

Routine prenatal labs are normal, including HIV and hepatitis C screening. We discussed neonatal monitoring after delivery for infants exposed to methadone, and the program has been contacted for coordination. We will see her every four weeks.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Headache in Pregnancy
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt ~17 wks pregnant calling about a migraine since this morning, her usual type - one side, throbbing, light bothers her. No vision changes other than light sensitivity, no swelling, no RUQ pain. Says BP at OB last week was normal. Took acetaminophen 1000 mg at 9am with partial relief.

Per PCP: OK to use one sumatriptan 50 mg today if still bad in an hour; rest in a dark room, fluids. Call OB or go to L&D if this headache is different from her usual or if she has visual changes, swelling, or the worst headache of her life. Pt verbalized understanding.

5:20pm pt messaged: took sumatriptan, headache gone.

documents.title: Obstetrics - Third Trimester Update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Update at 28 weeks 3 days (visit 8/27/2019). Pregnancy progressing normally. Fundal height appropriate, fetal heart tones normal. Glucose screen normal. Tdap given today.

Methadone continues at 60 mg daily without withdrawal symptoms; we are in touch with the program. Pediatrics consult arranged before delivery to plan newborn monitoring. Migraine frequency lower in pregnancy.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt 34 weeks pregnant. Inactivated quadrivalent influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Recommended in pregnancy. No prior reactions. VIS given. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Delivery Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received by fax)

Patient: Jill Woodward   DOB 10/16/1986
Admitted 11/16/2019 in spontaneous labor at 40w0d. Discharged 11/19/2019.

Delivery: normal spontaneous vaginal delivery 11/16/2019 of a healthy female infant. Uncomplicated labor. Estimated blood loss within normal range. Placenta delivered intact.

Postpartum course: uncomplicated. Breastfeeding well with lactation support. Methadone 60 mg daily continued throughout, coordinated with her program. Infant observed per newborn protocol and discharged with mother.

Discharge medications: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP), prenatal vitamin daily, ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: obstetrics postpartum visit at 6 weeks; primary care as scheduled.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE (received from regional hospital)
Date of service: 11/26/2019

Chief complaint: behaving strangely, confused; 10 days postpartum.

History is mostly from her husband. Patient is 33, delivered her first baby 10 days ago (uncomplicated vaginal delivery). Since coming home she has barely slept. Over several days she has become increasingly odd - he hears her talking to herself and she seems to be answering voices he can't hear. Tonight she told him the baby is possessed and that she has to protect her from evil spirits, which is what brought them in. No known head injury, fever or substance use; she has had her methadone at the program daily. Seen in this ED last December for appendicitis.

PMH: migraine without aura; opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg daily; appendectomy 12/2018.
Meds: methadone 60 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt with bipolar I; mother with postpartum depression and hypothyroidism.
SH: married, former smoker (quit 2015), no alcohol since entering treatment, works as administrative assistant at a community college.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Agitated, distracted, appears to be attending to internal stimuli. Oriented to person only - not to place or date. No focal neurologic deficit. Abdomen soft, fundus firm below umbilicus, lochia appropriate.

Labs: Hgb 12.5 g/dL, WBC 8.0 K, platelets 250 K. TSH 2.5. UA normal.

Impression: acute postpartum psychosis. Infant safe with husband and grandmother at home.
Plan: psychiatry consulted; voluntary admission to inpatient psychiatry accepted. Methadone dose confirmed with program for inpatient continuation.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Inpatient Psychiatry
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PSYCHIATRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY (released with patient consent)
Admission 11/27/2019 - Discharge 12/09/2019

Reason for admission: postpartum psychosis with onset in the first postpartum week - insomnia, auditory hallucinations, delusional belief that her newborn was possessed, disorientation.

Hospital course: Admitted voluntarily. Medical causes considered; ED labs including CBC, TSH and urinalysis were normal. Started olanzapine, titrated to 10 mg at bedtime. Sleep was protected with nursing support. Hallucinations faded over the first week, and by day 8 she was oriented, sleeping 7 hours, and had full insight that her beliefs about the baby had been part of an illness. She denied any thoughts of harming herself or the infant throughout. She pumped regularly on the unit and maintained her milk supply; olanzapine is considered compatible with breastfeeding and she plans to resume nursing at home. Husband and her mother participated in family meetings and will provide overnight infant care for the coming weeks so she can sleep.

Methadone 60 mg daily continued in coordination with her treatment program.

Mental status at discharge: calm, linear, euthymic, no perceptual disturbance, oriented x3, insight and judgment good.

Diagnosis: postpartum psychosis.
Discharge medications: olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime; methadone 60 mg daily (OTP); prenatal vitamin daily; sumatriptan as needed.
Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry 12/17; primary care within one week. Safety plan reviewed with patient and husband.

documents.title: Call From Family
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Husband called (on her release form) to let us know Jill was admitted overnight to inpatient psychiatry after the ED, 10 days after delivering. Says the baby is fine and with him and Jill's mother. Asked whether our office needs to do anything. Told him we would get the records and see her after discharge; gave the after-hours number. Routed to PCP.

PCP: thanks. Please book a visit within a week of discharge when we hear.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with husband and baby (26 days old). Discharged from inpatient psych 12/9 after admission for postpartum psychosis. Discharge summary reviewed.

She says she feels "like myself again, just tired." No voices since about a week into the admission. Understands what happened and is shaken by it. Sleeping 6-7 hrs - husband and her mom take the overnight feeds with pumped milk, she nurses during the day. Taking olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime every night. Methadone 60 mg, dosing at program, no cravings. Bleeding tapering. Breastfeeding going ok.

No thoughts of self-harm or harming the baby. Husband agrees she seems herself.

Exam: tired but bright, appropriate, linear, no evidence of responding to internal stimuli. Abdomen soft, nontender. PHQ-9 = 6 (sleep, energy, appetite items).

A/P
1. Postpartum psychosis, resolving on olanzapine - psychiatry f/u 12/17 confirmed. Keep protected sleep plan. Reviewed warning signs with both of them; they have our cell line and crisis numbers.
2. OUD in sustained remission - stable; program aware of admission.
3. Postpartum - OB visit at 6 weeks (12/30).
4. Weight still above pre-pregnancy, as expected 4 weeks after delivery.
See me in 4-6 weeks, sooner for any concern.

documents.title: Shaky and Heart Racing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I've felt really shaky and jittery since last weekend and my heart keeps pounding even when I'm sitting. Hard to focus on anything. I'm sleeping when I get the chance but it takes forever to fall asleep. My head feels clear otherwise - no voices or anything like that, I promise I'd tell you. Is this the olanzapine?? My mom says to ask about my thyroid because of my sister.

documents.title: Shaky and Heart Racing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me right away. Olanzapine doesn't usually do that. Your mom has a good point - thyroid inflammation after delivery is fairly common and causes exactly this. Please come Monday morning for blood work (thyroid and blood count); order is in. If your heart is racing with chest pain, fainting or trouble breathing, go to the ED. I'm also letting your psychiatrist know.

documents.title: Lab Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt. TSH 0.02 (suppressed), free T4 2.4 (high). CBC fine. Fits postpartum thyroiditis, thyrotoxic phase, though Graves is possible with her family history - uptake study will sort that out. Called endocrinology directly - they can see her 12/30, same day as her OB postpartum visit, so she only has to arrange childcare once.

Her watch shows a fast resting heart rate. No chest pain, no syncope. Advised to hold off on extra caffeine. Psychiatry FYI sent; she is still free of psychotic symptoms. She knows to go to the ED for chest pain, fainting or confusion.

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Seen 12/17/2019, eight days after discharge from inpatient care for postpartum psychosis. She is sleeping with family help and is euthymic, with no hallucinations or delusional thinking, good insight. Continuing olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime given how recent the episode was; we will revisit the dose in the new year. Aware of the new shakiness and racing heart and of your thyroid testing - agree this is more likely thyroid than psychiatric, and we'll follow it together.

Plan: continue olanzapine 10 mg nightly. Return every 2-3 weeks for now.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Obstetrics - Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward, DOB 10/16/1986
Visit 12/30/2019 - six-week postpartum examination

Ms. Woodward is 33 and returns six weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery of a healthy daughter. Her recovery from the birth itself has gone smoothly. Her postpartum period has been marked by an inpatient psychiatric admission for postpartum psychosis, now on olanzapine with good recovery, and by new symptoms suggesting thyroiditis, for which she sees endocrinology later today. She is exclusively breastfeeding.

History: migraine without aura; opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg; appendectomy 2018.
Medications: methadone 60 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin daily, sumatriptan as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 118/76. Breasts lactating, no masses or redness. Abdomen soft. Perineum healed. Uterus involuted, normal size. Exam otherwise unremarkable.
CBC and basic metabolic panel within normal limits.

Contraception: she does not want another pregnancy any time soon. We discussed options compatible with breastfeeding and chose the etonogestrel implant. Insertion is booked for a visit in late January.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth up to three times daily as needed for palpitations or tremor

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Patient: Jill Woodward   Seen: 12/30/2019; uptake study 12/31/2019
Requested by: primary care, for suppressed TSH six weeks postpartum

I saw Ms. Woodward this afternoon; she had her obstetric postpartum visit this morning. She delivered a healthy term daughter six weeks ago and is breastfeeding without difficulty. Around two weeks ago she began to feel restless with frequent palpitations and trouble keeping her focus, and her clothes have become looser although she is not trying to lose weight and her appetite is unchanged. No chest pain, dyspnea or recent illness. No anterior neck pain, no change in vision.

Recent history is notable for postpartum psychosis requiring a two-week admission, now on olanzapine and recovering well. Opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg daily. Migraine without aura.
Medications: methadone 60 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: sister with Hashimoto thyroiditis; mother with hypothyroidism.

Exam: HR 102 and regular. Fine tremor of both outstretched hands. Thyroid slightly enlarged and firm, not tender, no discrete nodule. No lid lag, no proptosis.

Data: TSH 0.02, free T4 2.4 (12/23, drawn by primary care). Radioactive iodine (I-123) uptake 12/31 is low. She pumped and discarded milk for the interval nuclear medicine advised and has resumed nursing.

Impression: thyrotoxicosis with low uptake six weeks after delivery - postpartum thyroiditis, thyrotoxic phase. Low uptake argues against Graves disease. This is a destructive, self-limited process; antithyroid drugs would not help.

Plan:
- Propranolol 10 mg up to three times a day as needed for palpitations and tremor; compatible with breastfeeding.
- Repeat thyroid tests in about six weeks. Many patients pass through a hypothyroid phase in the following months; I will see her again then.
- Copy to obstetrics and psychiatry.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update - the propranolol is helping a lot, I only take it once or twice a day now and my hands are steadier. I ended up cancelling the implant appointment for this week, I just can't do one more appointment right now with the baby and all the doctor visits. I'll reschedule when things calm down.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad the propranolol is helping. Totally understand about the appointment. One thing to keep in mind: nursing protects against pregnancy only for a while and not reliably once feeds space out or your period comes back, so please do rebook with OB before then. Endocrinology will recheck your thyroid next month.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning on an empty stomach

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP   Seen 2/10/2020

Ms. Woodward returns six weeks after her first visit, now about three months postpartum and still breastfeeding. The jitteriness and palpitations settled within a few weeks and she stopped needing propranolol. Over the last several weeks, though, she has felt more tired than usual even on nights she sleeps well, has trouble concentrating, and has gained some weight. Appetite unchanged. She feels more emotionally sensitive but denies depressive thoughts. She remains well psychiatrically on olanzapine.

Medications: methadone 60 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, propranolol 10 mg as needed (not using), sumatriptan as needed.

Exam: vital signs normal. Thyroid not enlarged today, no nodules, not tender. Heart and lungs normal. Reflexes and neurologic exam unremarkable.

Labs today: TSH 14.2, free T4 0.6. Thyroid peroxidase antibodies not detected.

Impression: postpartum thyroiditis, now in the hypothyroid phase. Antibody-negative, which favors eventual recovery.

Plan:
- Stop propranolol.
- Start levothyroxine 50 mcg daily given symptoms and breastfeeding; safe while nursing.
- TSH and free T4 in about six weeks - primary care may draw and send to me.
- Plan a trial off levothyroxine at roughly 12 months postpartum.
- Because of this episode she has an ongoing risk of permanent hypothyroidism; a yearly TSH is reasonable after recovery.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Thyroid Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH 3.4, free T4 1.1 on levothyroxine 50 mcg - back in range. Message sent to pt; copy faxed to endocrinology. Continue current dose.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit (pt at home, daughter on her lap). Campus closed, working from home.

Mood good. Sleeping well, husband still does one night feed. No psychotic symptoms since December. Seeing psychiatry by video; still on olanzapine 10 at night, they plan to lower it soon. Energy better since starting levothyroxine; labs last week normal. No palpitations. Methadone 60 mg - program switched her to more take-home doses during the shutdown, managing them fine and keeps them locked. Naloxone at home. Breastfeeding, baby gaining well per pediatrician. One migraine in March.

Exam: limited to video, well-appearing, bright, linear thought, normal speech.

PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 3.

A/P
- Postpartum psychosis, in remission on olanzapine - psych managing.
- Postpartum thyroiditis, hypothyroid phase - levothyroxine 50 per endocrinology, TSH at goal.
- OUD in remission - stable.
- Migraine - stable.
- Implant not yet placed; she will call OB once their office reopens for procedures.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Seen by video 4/14/2020. Remains in full remission from postpartum psychosis - no perceptual changes, mood stable, sleeping well. Given four months of sustained remission, olanzapine reduced to 5 mg at bedtime today. Plan to continue treatment through roughly the first postpartum year, then taper if she stays well.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Obstetrics - Breast Lump Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward   Seen 6/2/2020

Ms. Woodward, 33, is six months postpartum and exclusively breastfeeding. Over the past several weeks she has noticed a slowly enlarging, mildly uncomfortable swelling in the outer part of the right breast. It does not change in size with feeding. No fever, chills or nipple discharge.

History: postpartum psychosis (in remission, on olanzapine), postpartum thyroiditis now on levothyroxine, migraine, opioid use disorder in remission on methadone.
Medications: methadone 60 mg, olanzapine 5 mg nightly, levothyroxine 50 mcg, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Temperature 36.8 C (98.2 F); other vitals normal.
Right breast: smooth, fluctuant, mobile mass about 4 cm just lateral to the areola. No redness or warmth, not tender. No axillary lymph nodes. Left breast normal.

Assessment: galactocele, right breast.
Plan: ultrasound to confirm. Continue breastfeeding - no need to stop. If it becomes uncomfortable it can be aspirated. Rebooking the implant visit for later this summer.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

reports.text: Indication: palpable mass lateral to the right areola in a lactating patient. Targeted ultrasound of the right breast at the site of palpable concern, 9 o'clock periareolar. There is a 4.0 cm circumscribed oval cystic lesion with a fat-fluid level and no internal vascularity on color Doppler. No solid component. Surrounding fibroglandular tissue shows lactational change. Right axilla: normal lymph nodes.
reports.conclusion: 4.0 cm circumscribed cystic lesion with fat-fluid level at the site of palpable concern, consistent with galactocele. BI-RADS 2: benign.

documents.title: Breast Ultrasound Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Outside breast ultrasound report received from radiology (ordered by OB), scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Breast Ultrasound
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The ultrasound report says BI-RADS 2 - I googled it and now I'm worried. Is it ok? OB office hasn't called me yet.

documents.title: Breast Ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: It's good news. BI-RADS 2 means benign - the scan shows a milk-filled cyst (galactocele), exactly what your OB thought. Nothing else needs to be done unless it bothers you, in which case they can drain it. Keep nursing as you have been.

events.reason: Left lower abdominal pain, vaginal spotting

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received from regional hospital)
Date of service: 08/18/2020

CC: sudden left lower abdominal pain, spotting

HPI: 33 y/o, nine months postpartum and still breastfeeding, not yet using contraception after counseling earlier this year. Sharp left-sided pain that began abruptly 4 hours ago. Light vaginal spotting for 2 days. LMP 6 weeks ago; cycles regular at 28 days. History of migraine, postpartum psychosis (in remission), postpartum thyroiditis, OUD in remission on methadone. Prior laparoscopic appendectomy.

Meds: methadone 60 mg daily, olanzapine 5 mg nightly, levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.0 C (98.6 F). Anxious, clearly in distress. LLQ tenderness with rebound. Speculum: cervical os closed, no active bleeding. Bimanual: cervical motion tenderness.

Labs: quantitative hCG 2500 mIU/mL. Hgb 9.8 g/dL, Hct 29%. WBC 12.0 K, plt 250 K.
Bedside US: no intrauterine pregnancy; complex left adnexal mass; moderate free fluid in the pelvis.

Assessment: ruptured left ectopic pregnancy with hemoperitoneum, hemodynamically unstable.
Plan: 2 large-bore IVs, fluid bolus, type and cross, emergent OB/GYN consult. To OR.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food for 3 months
medications.reason: Blood loss from ruptured ectopic pregnancy

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain
Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours with food as needed for pain, up to 5 days

reports.text: Specimen: left fallopian tube, salpingectomy. Gross: segment of fallopian tube with a ruptured, hemorrhagic dilated portion and attached blood clot. Microscopic: chorionic villi and trophoblast within the tubal lumen and wall with extensive hemorrhage and rupture of the tubal wall. No molar change.
reports.conclusion: Left fallopian tube with chorionic villi and hemorrhage, consistent with ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Gynecology
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 08/18/2020 - Discharged 08/20/2020
Diagnosis: ruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy with hemoperitoneum
Procedure: emergency laparoscopic left salpingectomy, evacuation of hemoperitoneum, 08/18/2020

Brought to the OR directly from the ED. Hemoperitoneum evacuated; ruptured left tubal pregnancy identified and the left tube removed. Right tube and both ovaries normal. Appendectomy site unremarkable. Blood pressure and heart rate normalized after fluid resuscitation and control of bleeding. Post-op course uneventful.

Methadone 60 mg continued, confirmed with her program. Pain controlled with acetaminophen and ibuprofen. Continued olanzapine and levothyroxine. She may continue breastfeeding.

Pathology: chorionic villi in the left tube with rupture, consistent with ectopic pregnancy.

Discharge medications: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily for 3 months (new), acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed, methadone 60 mg daily (OTP), olanzapine 5 mg nightly, levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: gynecology in 4 weeks with hCG; contraception will be addressed then. PCP within one week. Emotional support resources given.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge 8/20 (lap L salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic). Pain manageable on acetaminophen/ibuprofen. Up and walking, drinking well, started iron. Port sites clean. Tearful when talking about it - says she didn't even know she was pregnant. Husband home with her this week. Appt with PCP 8/26. Reviewed when to call/ED: fainting, worsening pain, fever, heavy bleeding.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. Ruptured L tubal ectopic 8/18, emergency lap L salpingectomy, home 8/20. Records reviewed.

Feeling stronger each day. Pain minimal, acetaminophen once a day. Taking iron daily. Still nursing. Sad about the pregnancy loss and shaken by how fast it happened; sleeping ok, no intrusive thoughts, mood otherwise steady. Talked to her psychiatrist this week, who did not change anything. Methadone at program, no cravings, husband taking her to dosing until she can drive.

Exam: BP and HR normal, afebrile. Port sites healing well, no erythema. Abdomen soft, minimal tenderness.
Hgb today 10.4 (9.8 preop in ED).

A/P
1. S/p ruptured ectopic, L salpingectomy - recovering. Gyn f/u 9/17 with hCG; she wants the implant placed then.
2. Blood loss - Hgb improving; iron x 3 months, recheck CBC in a few months.
3. Grief after pregnancy loss - normal reaction, PHQ-9 4. Watching closely with her history; psychiatry aware.
4. Postpartum thyroiditis on levothyroxine, psychosis in remission on olanzapine 5 - per specialists.

medications.sig: Subdermal implant, left upper arm, placed 9/17/2020

documents.title: Gynecology - Post-op Visit and Implant Insertion
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward   Seen 9/17/2020

Four weeks after emergency laparoscopic left salpingectomy for a ruptured tubal pregnancy. Recovering well; incisions healed. Serum hCG has returned to negative. Hemoglobin improving on iron per her primary care labs. Discussed what the loss of one tube means for future fertility (the remaining tube is normal) and the higher chance of ectopic in any future pregnancy - she should have an early ultrasound if she conceives again.

She requested the etonogestrel implant, which was placed today in the left upper arm under local anesthesia without complication. Palpable after placement. Effective for at least three years.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Seen 10/6/2020. Now over ten months from the onset of postpartum psychosis with sustained full remission, including through the stress of her recent ectopic pregnancy and surgery. Grieving appropriately, functioning well, sleep intact. After discussion she preferred to stop medication, and olanzapine was tapered and discontinued at this visit. Relapse signs reviewed with her and her husband. We will see her twice more before discharge to your care.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Masked, screened at door. No prior reaction. VIS given. Pt breastfeeding - ok to vaccinate. Fine after observation.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP (telehealth)   11/12/2020

Now about twelve months postpartum and feeling well on levothyroxine 50 mcg. Last TSH in range. Thyroid antibodies were negative. Interval ectopic pregnancy and surgery in August noted, recovered; implant placed in September.

Plan: stop levothyroxine now. TSH and free T4 in 6 weeks (primary care to draw). If normal, no further treatment; yearly TSH going forward, and testing early in any future pregnancy and again after delivery, since postpartum thyroiditis tends to recur.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Discharge
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Jill Woodward

Final visit 12/15/2020. Two months off olanzapine with no return of symptoms; mood euthymic, sleep normal. Diagnosis: postpartum psychosis, in full remission. She is discharged to primary care.

Recommendations: if she considers another pregnancy, please refer her for perinatal psychiatry consultation before conception, as the risk of recurrence after a future delivery is substantial and a prevention plan should be in place. Return sooner for any sleep loss, mood change or unusual thoughts.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news to end the year: your thyroid is normal off the levothyroxine (TSH 2.6), so your thyroid has recovered. Your blood count is back up to 12.6 - you've finished the iron and don't need more. I sent a copy to endocrinology. Let's do a video visit in January to tidy up your problem list now that psychiatry and endocrinology have both signed off.
